papers.title: Shox2 maintains thalamocortical neuron firing for whisker-based somatomotor responses and sleep spindles in mice
papers.summary: Using genetic labeling, optogenetics, and conditional knockout in mouse VPM thalamus, the authors show that Shox2 is required to maintain intrinsic tonic and burst firing of thalamocortical neurons without altering circuit organization. Shox2 loss impaired whisker-dependent somatomotor performance and reduced cortical sleep spindle density, identifying a transcriptional regulator linking firing modes to spindle deficits.

papers.title: WakeSentry: real-time awakening detection from single-channel EEG across sleep cohorts and forehead headbands
papers.summary: The authors developed WakeSentry, a real-time single-channel frontal EEG awakening detector trained on past EEG and evaluated on 1,529 PSG nights from five cohorts and 224 headband nights. At 0.5 false awakenings per hour it raised PSG awakening sensitivity from 63.8% to 70.5% and headband sensitivity from 49.8% to 53.9%, outperforming GSSC in every cohort and enabling a closed-loop stimulation gate.

papers.title: NED-Net: open-source software for building and refining seizure detectors during rodent EEG experiments
papers.summary: The authors introduce NED-Net, open-source software for training and maintaining rodent EEG seizure detectors through an annotation-training loop that retrains on reviewed candidate events as annotations accumulate. A detector trained on one mouse cohort reached 93.6% precision, but failed to generalize (median per-animal recall 10%), and retraining with second-cohort annotations raised convulsive recall from 15% to 64%, detecting at least one reference seizure in every animal.

papers.title: Nsun5 deficiency leads to impaired myelin integrity and sleep disruption.
papers.summary: In Nsun5-knockout mice, loss of 28S rRNA m5C caused selective translational dysregulation of myelination and voltage-gated potassium channel programs (e.g., Kcna1/Kcna2), with oligodendrocyte loss, corpus callosum hypomyelination, and reduced non-REM sleep. Clemastine improved sleep abnormalities and myelin integrity, and 4-aminopyridine also alleviated the sleep phenotype, linking rRNA methylation to white-matter dysfunction and sleep disruption.

papers.title: Targeting memory consolidation in major depression via pharmacological slow-wave sleep promotion
papers.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 22 MDD patients and 20 matched controls tested single nocturnal doses of GHB and trazodone with polysomnography and pre/post-sleep memory testing. GHB strongly increased slow-wave sleep duration and delta power, but neither drug improved declarative, procedural, or emotional memory consolidation, challenging the assumption that increasing SWS alone improves overnight memory.

papers.title: MLE EEG Toolbox: A Personal AI Laboratory Assistant for Literature-Informed and Reproducible M/EEG Research
papers.summary: The authors present MLE EEG Toolbox, a locally deployed AI framework integrating natural-language-guided M/EEG analysis, literature retrieval, validated operation selection, and computational provenance for reproducibility. It achieved action-selection accuracies of 85.6% for EEG and 95.5% for MEG, with 142 cross-platform tests showing close numerical agreement and demonstrated spectral, network, decoding, and source analyses on public datasets.

papers.title: A Soft Sponge-Pillar Electrode Platform for Motion-Tolerant Ambulatory EEG and Sleep Monitoring.
papers.summary: Developed a soft carbon black–PDMS sponge-pillar EEG electrode, fabricated by sugar templating, that bypasses hair with a firm base and uses a porous conductive-gel-loaded tip for low-modulus, high-area scalp contact. It achieved 1.62×10^4 Ω contact impedance at 10 Hz with gel stability over 18 h and recorded EEG during motion (headbands, headphones, caps) at 16.46 dB SNR.

papers.title: Sleep-Deprivation Serum Induces Mitochondrial Stress in BV2 Cells: Responses to P2Y12-Targeted Pharmacological Modulation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Using an in vitro serum-transfer model, serum from sleep-deprived mice reduced mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 ratio), shortened mitochondrial networks, and suppressed Rhod-2 calcium responses in BV2 microglia. P2Y12 antagonist MRS2395 and agonist 2-MeSADP failed to consistently restore mitochondrial or calcium response profiles under sleep-deprivation serum, linking sleep-loss circulating factors to microglial mitochondrial stress and altered purinergic responsiveness.

papers.title: Circadian feeding rhythm loss drives sex-specific β-cell dysfunction in diet-induced obesity.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Exposed male and female C57BL/6 mice to high-fat diet for eight weeks and assessed circadian feeding/activity, glucose tolerance, insulin secretion, islet RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, testing time-restricted feeding. DIO disrupted circadian fasting/feeding and abolished circadian glucose tolerance and GSIS in males but not females, reduced circadian-regulated islet transcripts by 42.1%, and dark-phase tRF restored circadian glucose tolerance, GSIS and islet gene expression.

papers.title: Psychedelics and Sleep: Preclinical and Human Studies-A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided systematic review of 12 preclinical and clinical studies found that classic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT/ayahuasca) consistently produce acute REM sleep suppression, delayed REM onset, and increased wakefulness in preclinical work, with heterogeneous human findings including prolonged REM latency after psilocybin and reduced REM duration after ayahuasca. Evidence on slow-wave activity was mixed, and included studies showed fair-to-poor validity and notable risk of bias.

papers.title: Spikes in the night: rapid eye movement sleep maximally attenuates epileptiform spike morphology.
papers.summary: Quantified nine morphological features of 7379 interictal epileptiform discharges across sleep-wake states in 17 adults with focal epilepsy using continuous video-EEG telemetry. REM IEDs showed the shallowest slopes, bluntest peaks, and smallest amplitudes/area, while awake IEDs were steepest and spikiest, indicating maximal attenuation of epileptiform morphology in REM.

papers.title: Circadian modulation of dopamine release shapes reward-evoked signaling in the nucleus accumbens.
papers.summary: Long-term fiber photometry with the DA3m sensor in C57BL/6J mice showed that spontaneous nucleus accumbens dopamine peaked in the early subjective day, reward-evoked dopamine peaked at the day-to-night transition, and cue-evoked dopamine and reward behavior peaked in the early subjective night. SCN-specific Bmal1 disruption attenuated spontaneous dopamine rhythmicity, and reward-evoked dopamine was positively associated with reward behavior and cue-evoked dopamine but negatively associated with pre-reward baseline dopamine.

papers.title: NeuroSim: a clinically informed multi-disorder EEG simulator with personalized pattern injection and AI-driven neurological modeling
papers.summary: Presented NeuroSim, a clinically informed simulator generating synthetic multichannel EEG with user-controlled, region- and severity-specific disease pattern injection across AD, PD, schizophrenia, epilepsy and FTD. A convolutional-attention classifier trained on simulated data reached 95.3–96.8% hold-out accuracy, and augmenting real clinical EEG with NeuroSim samples raised AD-vs-control accuracy from 91.6% to 94.5% and PD-vs-control from 90.9% to 94.0%.

papers.title: Seizure Prediction Using Channel-Optimized Intracranial EEG With Variable Interictal and Preictal Durations.
papers.journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
papers.summary: Evaluated seizure prediction on intracranial EEG using six combinations of interictal (24 h, 48 h) and preictal (30, 60, 90 min) durations and three classification strategies including channel-optimization-based majority voting. On the SWEC-ETHZ dataset the method reached up to 87.7% sensitivity, 94.6% specificity, 0.912 AUC at segment level and 95.9% sensitivity with 0.05/h FPR at event level, with channel optimization outperforming all-channel and single-channel strategies.

papers.title: Two Axes of Sleep, One Heart: Dissociating Objective Sleep-Disordered Breathing From Subjective Sleep Duration in Cardiac Risk
papers.summary: Tested whether objective sleep-disordered breathing (8,444 polysomnograms) and subjective sleep duration (407,303 BRFSS adults) carry separable cardiac risk information using regression, dose-response, and comorbidity-network analyses. Both short (<7 h) and long (>9 h) sleep were associated with heart attack (AORs 1.24 and 1.30) and stroke (1.12 and 1.42), with U-shaped dose-response and increased comorbidity-network density under suboptimal sleep.

papers.title: Influence of social housing on dim light at night induced behavioural and hepatic alterations in mice.
papers.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
papers.summary: In male mice exposed to dim light at night (DLAN) or a standard light-dark cycle for 28 days, social isolation exacerbated DLAN-induced anxiety-like behaviour, anhedonia, oxidative stress, and hepatic injury, whereas group housing attenuated these behavioural and hepatic deficits and improved antioxidant status.

papers.title: Disentangling Monitor Hardware Artifacts and Smoothing Lag for Shift-Robust Intraoperative EEG and Hemodynamic Risk Calibration
papers.summary: Developed a causal signal-conditioning and shift-robust conformal calibration framework for intraoperative EEG and hemodynamic risk forecasting across 5,439 anesthesia procedures. Pre-filter blanking removed ~97.9% and ~97.6% of false flatline conflicts while preserving ~99.2% and ~99.0% of deep suppression, and Subgroup-Covariate-Weighted conformal risk control bounded all 70 TIVA shift cells at ≤4.38% (alpha=5.0%) in 66.32 ms per 30-s epoch.

papers.title: Effects of Environmental Enrichment on the Behavior of Scarlet Macaws (Ara macao cyanopterus) for Reintroduction.
papers.summary: Evaluated environmental enrichment effects on behaviors relevant to wild survival and on abnormal behaviors in hand-reared scarlet macaws in the pre-release phase, comparing pre-enrichment and enrichment phases with Wilcoxon tests and association indices. Enrichment significantly increased exploration and group cohesion, decreased resting, self-care, and abnormal behaviors, and yielded more individuals with high release-suitability scores, without changing flight behavior.

papers.title: Frontal Low-Frequency Electroencephalographic Coherence in Bipolar Disorder: A Covariate-Controlled Secondary Analysis of a Public Resting-State EEG Feature Dataset.
papers.summary: Tested frontal/frontopolar low-frequency resting-state EEG coherence in bipolar disorder versus healthy controls, depressive disorder, and schizophrenia in a covariate-controlled secondary analysis of a public dataset (n=472). Bipolar disorder showed higher adjusted delta/theta coherence than all comparison groups (partial η2=.037-.040), with effects strongest in frontopolar pairs and attenuated when anterior electrodes were excluded.

papers.title: Characterizing source-level electroencephalography activities to single-pulse TMS-EEG.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Compared active versus sham single-pulse TMS-EEG over the left DLPFC in 33 healthy adults using source-level current density (SCD) and scattering (SCS) measures. Active stimulation produced larger early local TEPs (2.15 vs. 0.85 μV) and greater target-region SCS/SCD in both early and late windows, while whole-brain clusters were significant only at late latencies and partly attenuated after muscle-related covariate adjustment.

papers.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG sleep staging using a serpentine dataflow that reduces memory accesses 6.2× and 2.25× over output- and weight-stationary dataflows, plus hybrid dynamic quantization reducing model size 4.16×. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, it consumes 0.40 mW and stays within 0.15% of floating-point accuracy on MASS-SS3 leave-two-subject-out validation.

papers.title: Neural Entropy Pattern : An EEG Representation for Predicting Depression Therapy Outcomes.
papers.summary: Proposes the Neural Entropy Pattern (NEP), an EEG representation of ten entropy measures from 19 channels and five frequency bands plus broadband, used with deep and shallow classifiers to predict depression therapy response. Best balanced accuracy was 76.4% (AUC 0.89) for SSRI under LOSO with EfficientNet-B0 and 63.7% for rTMS; log-energy and differential entropy carried most Shapley importance.

papers.title: Group-specific associations among sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry in college students: evidence from a cross-sectional EEG study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional EEG study of 120 college students comparing 60 with elevated depressive symptoms to 60 controls, examining associations among sleep quality (PSQI), depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA). The depressive-symptom group had worse PSQI scores and lower composite FAA, and FAA correlated with PSQI and depressive symptoms only in that group; a BMI-adjusted model explained R2=0.243.

papers.title: Integrated roles of regulatory non-coding RNAs in circadian gene expression and disease pathogenesis.
papers.summary: Reviews recent progress on microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and circular RNAs in circadian rhythm regulation and their dysfunction in pathological conditions including cancer, metabolic disorders, and neurological disease. Emphasizes an integrative cross-ncRNA-class view and context-specific gene regulation, noting circRNA mechanisms remain emerging.

papers.title: Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice.
papers.summary: In male mice exposed to intermittent hypoxia for 7–210 days, the authors found tissue-specific DNA methylation changes (5,747 DMPs in left ventricle, 1,307 in PBMCs) and epigenetic age acceleration, with Cdkn2a/p16 senescence implicated in vascular dysfunction. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve.

papers.title: Improved sleep and clinical outcomes following a single-session intervention among adolescents with borderline personality disorder features.
papers.summary: Intervention trial (NCT04507308) in 57 adolescents with borderline personality disorder features and sleep difficulties testing a single-session sleep-focused treatment informed by the Transdiagnostic Sleep and Circadian Intervention. Many objective (EEG) and subjective sleep indices improved post-treatment and at one-month follow-up, and multiple BPD symptom indices also improved significantly.

papers.title: Circadian disruption worsens postseptic pulmonary fibrotic remodeling through a CLOCK/PIEZO1-linked myeloid immunometabolic program.
papers.summary: Using patient lung specimens, murine transcriptomic datasets, and cecal ligation and puncture with shifted light-dark cycles, this study showed that circadian disruption suppresses macrophage CLOCK, derepresses PIEZO1, impairs lipophagy, and promotes PAD4-dependent extracellular trap formation, aggravating post-septic pulmonary fibrosis; myeloid Piezo1 deletion attenuated fibrosis.

papers.title: Supraorbital Near-Infrared Stimulation and Portable EEG: An Exploratory Fixed-Order Study of Spectral Markers and Signal Quality.
papers.summary: Exploratory fixed-order study in 25 healthy women comparing active 940-nm supraorbital near-infrared stimulation at Visit 1 with sham at Visit 2, using portable MUSE 2 EEG. Global gamma log-power PRE-to-DURING difference-in-change was 0.101 a.u. (paired t-test p=0.040) but not significant by Wilcoxon (p=0.090), with visit-order confounding and unverified signal origin precluding stimulation-effect conclusions.

papers.title: Circadian Regulation of Gastrointestinal Physiology and Disease: Mechanisms, Chrononutrition, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates molecular clock mechanisms with clinical evidence on circadian regulation of gastrointestinal physiology and disease, covering chrononutrition and chronomodulated chemotherapy. It emphasizes that meal-timing effects on metabolic markers do not consistently exceed calorie restriction and that sleep-intervention trials have not established relapse prevention, highlighting the need for controlled trials assessing biological phase and disease activity.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation remodels hepatic immune microenvironment via circadian gene dysregulation and promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression.
papers.summary: Using GEO transcriptomic datasets, a rat sleep-deprivation model, machine learning, and immune-infiltration analyses, this study identified six core circadian rhythm-related genes (Cirbp, Srebf1, Fbxo31, Hsp90aa1, Btc, Dlgap1) mediating sleep deprivation-induced hepatic immune remodeling. Cirbp and Hsp90aa1 were associated with immune infiltration and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma, and Serpine1 was independently identified as a key sleep deprivation-related gene.

papers.title: Analysis of nighttime heart rate variability during rapid eye movement and non-rapid eye movement in OSA.
papers.summary: In a retrospective polysomnography study of 373 patients with OSA, REM-related OSA in males with mild-to-moderate disease was independently associated with lower LFnu and LF/HF and higher HFnu during N1 and N2 sleep, whereas autonomic differences were absent in women and in REM sleep, indicating sex- and severity-dependent autonomic profiles.

papers.title: Depressive symptoms moderate daily anticipated and momentary emotion dynamics and associate with complex brain network topology: Resting-state EEG and ecological momentary assessment evidence.
papers.summary: Combining resting-state EEG with a 14-day ecological momentary assessment in 96 young adults, this study found that anticipated emotion prospectively predicted momentary positive emotion (β = .191) and inversely predicted negative emotion (β = -.125), with depressive symptoms moderating this link above PHQ-9 scores of roughly 5.7-9.7. Theta and delta band minimum spanning tree topology was indirectly associated with daily emotional dynamics via baseline depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation, Occupational Stress, and Work-related Determinants of Sleep Disturbance Among Practicing Physicians: A Cross-sectional Study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional survey of 627 practicing physicians assessing sleep patterns, lifestyle, and work-related stressors, finding that 54.1% slept ≤6 hours per night and 51.9% had sleep disturbance at least twice weekly. Sleep deprivation and disturbance were associated with work-related stressors such as poor work-life balance and administrative burden rather than lifestyle factors.

papers.title: Exploring the genetic determinants of ALS in a North Indian cohort using a genomic screening approach
papers.summary: In 73 clinically diagnosed ALS patients from North India, targeted sequencing, repeat expansion analysis, and whole exome sequencing identified a pathogenic TARDBP variant, one C9orf72 expansion, pathogenic ATXN1 expansions, and rare variants in ANXA11, SIGMAR1, SETX, ERBB4, and NEK1. Poor sleep quality and excessive daytime sleepiness were frequent but not significantly associated with disease severity.

papers.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
papers.summary: Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational microlongitudinal feasibility protocol for 25 mother-child dyads (children aged 11-14) combining Garmin wearables, passive smartphone sensing, ecological momentary assessment, and mobile cognitive testing over 4 weeks to assess feasibility and explore within-person and dyadic associations among health behaviors, cognition, and momentary anxiety.

papers.title: Epilepsy Surgery in Patients with Non-Lesional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Evaluated with Stereoelectroencephalography: Retrospective Analysis in a High-Complexity Center and Literature Review.
papers.summary: This retrospective series of 11 patients with non-lesional MRI epilepsy evaluated by stereoelectroencephalography reported that SEEG localized the epileptogenic zone in all patients, with 63.6% achieving good postoperative outcomes; extratemporal non-lesional cases showed better outcomes than temporal cases.

papers.title: Vestibular Epilepsy Presenting With Isolated Recurrent Vertigo and Postictal Headache: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report of a 38-year-old woman with recurrent brief vertigo and postictal headache, diagnosed with vestibular epilepsy after EEG showed generalized epileptiform discharges and divalproex sodium markedly reduced attack frequency.

papers.title: Changes in negative affect and resting-state EEG power following an EEG-derived generative reality art experience: a pilot pre-post study.
papers.summary: Exploratory pilot pre-post study of 30 healthy university students examined an EEG-derived generative virtual reality art experience, finding decreased negative affect and reduced resting-state absolute alpha- and beta-band power after a single 5-minute session. Changes in EEG measures were not associated with affect changes, and the single-group design precludes causal or therapeutic conclusions.

papers.title: The regenerative hexagon: six domains shaping musculoskeletal regenerative outcomes.
papers.summary: Proposes a "Regenerative Hexagon" framework that extends the classical scaffold-cells-growth factors triad with three host-state domains (Systemic Host Environment, Biomechanics/Mechanotransduction, Cellular Energetics), and grades evidence for each component, hypothesizing multiplicative interactions among pillars. Frames the model as a hypothesis-generating instrument rather than a validated clinical tool.

papers.title: Statement of Retraction: Alterations in circadian rhythms aggravate Acetaminophen-induced liver injury in mice by influencing Acetaminophen metabolization and increasing intestinal permeability.
papers.summary: This is a retraction notice for a previously published article on circadian rhythm alterations and acetaminophen-induced liver injury in mice; no abstract or findings are provided.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
